messages:
emma: Quick sync — we need to lock final owners and minimal acceptance criteria for the upcoming launch window. Items: SLA tiers, supported degradation modes, docs quickstart + migration notes, monitoring dashboards + burn-in alerts, pricing examples + cost-guard rails, support runbook + oncall training. Drop 'i'll own X' here.

raj: i'll own monitoring + runbook integration. plan: 1) dashboard for p50/p95/p99 latency by model variant, 2) token burn rate chart, 3) alert on sustained p99 > 1.2s for 10m. also want an operational test that simulates cache misses.

claire: i'll take docs quickstart + migration notes. will add a short agnostic "Optimizing for cost & latency" section for customers moving from hosted->dedicated. ETA: tomorrow noon.

tom: i'll own pricing examples and cost guardrail language. need clear examples for three customer profiles (startup, scale SaaS, enterprise). also propose a billing note about metered tokens vs preview tokens.

emma: For SLA, we need wording for hosted/dedicated and also a burst/fallback clause. Looking for someone to draft SLA text + accepted exceptions.

raj: tagging SLA: i'll draft the exception cases in parallel with monitoring so the SLOs align with alerting. proposal: hosted default 99.9% availability monthly, dedicated negotiated minimum 99.7% with burst tolerances. include a fallback clause: "automatic fallback to compatible model variant during capacity pressure; customers notified via headers and postmortem if systematic."

claire: question on docs — should we include a short "what to expect during bursts" FAQ in the quickstart or the migration guide? Feels like quickstart is better for customer-facing handoff.

tom: put the economics examples in pricing page and link them in quickstart. For cost-guard rails, recommend a soft cap + alert to admins when projected monthly spend > threshold and an auto-throttle option.

ops-bot: runbook-helper: template updated — /runbook scaffold preflight-launch v3 available at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/preflight-v3. Reminder: include recovery steps < 15m/>30m/>1h.

emma: Good. Action recap: SLA text + exceptions — raj (draft by EOD); Docs quickstart + migration — claire (tom will review pricing examples); Monitoring & tests + runbook links — raj; Pricing examples + billing notes — tom; Oncall training session — emma will schedule Wed 10:00 PT.

raj: ack. I'll also add an automated soak test job to run during dry-run window and post results to the launch channel.

claire: ack. I'll add a tiny snippet for "how to interpret our latency charts" so customers know p50 vs p99 tradeoffs.

tom: ack. Will prepare three sample invoices and a short FAQ about reserved capacity credits.

emma: We'll run a full dry-run Fri 08:00 PT. Please have PRs or draft links before Thurs EOD. If any blockers, escalate in #release-war-room. Thanks all.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: docs build succeeded for main at 1776004600.

emma: P.S. include a paragraph in SLA about telemetry retention for compliance customers (30/90/365 day options) so support knows expectations.
